paraphrase: The exaltations of the Sun and the rest are Aries, Taurus, Capricorn, Virgo, Cancer, Pisces and Libra, at the 10th, 3rd, 28th, 15th, 5th, 27th and 20th degrees; their falls are in the seventh sign from these.

paraphrase: The houses from the ascendant are named body (tanu), family, co-born, kin, son, enemy, wife, death, fortune (śubha), position, gain and loss (riḥpha); the 3rd, 6th, 10th and 11th are 'increasing' (upacaya). The 4th and 8th are 'quadrangular'; the 1st, 4th, 7th and 10th are the angles (kaṇṭaka, kendra, catuṣṭaya), in which planets are strong; after an angle comes the paṇaphara and then the āpoklima. The 4th is also hibuka, the 7th jāmitra, the 10th meṣūraṇa or karma.

paraphrase: The Yavanas counted the yogas of the sky (nābhasa) as eighteen hundred; they are treated here in brief. When all planets occupy movable, fixed or dual signs the āśraya yogas rajju, musala and nala arise; when benefics or malefics occupy the angles, the two dala yogas, the garland (mālā) and the serpent (sarpa), which Parāśara described.

paraphrase: When four or more strong planets are together in one sign, the native becomes a renunciant; according to the strongest of them — Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, the Moon, Venus, Saturn or the Sun — he becomes a Śākya (Buddhist), an Ājīvika, a bhikṣu, a vṛddha (elder ascetic), a caraka, a nirgrantha (Jain) or a forest-dweller living on wild food. If the lord of that renunciation is overcome by others, he falls from it.

paraphrase: If the planets giving renunciation are overpowered by the Sun's rays, the persons are not initiated but are devoted to that order; if weak and aspected by others they are initiated only on request. One obtains initiation (dīkṣā) when the unaspected lord of the birth-sign looks at Saturn, or Saturn looks at the weak lord of the birth-sign, or the Moon in Saturn's decan or in a navāṃśa of Mars or Saturn is aspected by Saturn. With Jupiter, the Moon and the ascendant aspected by Saturn and Jupiter in the ninth, one born in a royal yoga becomes a founder of a holy place (tīrthakṛt); with Saturn in the ninth, a consecrated king.

paraphrase: Of Kāla, the Sun is the self, the Moon the mind, Mars strength, Mercury speech, Jupiter knowledge and happiness, Venus desire, Saturn sorrow. The Sun and Moon are kings, Mars the general, Mercury the prince, Jupiter and Venus ministers, Saturn the servant.
